question.leadin: This man refused to recant his writings at the Diet of Worms.
question.text: Name this German theologian, who, angered by the Catholic Church's use of indulgences, launched the Protestant Reformation by publishing his Ninety-FIve Theses.
question.clue: Those pitfalls may have caused him to write such pamphlets as Against the Heavenly Prophets and Against the Jews and Their Lies.

swap.leadin: This leader was nicknamed the "Iron Chancellor" for conducting diplomacy using the strategy of Realpolitik.
swap.text: Name this Prussian statesman, who masterminded the Unification of Germany.
swap.clue: This man modified Count Benedetti's words in the doctored Ems Dispatch to instigate a war between his country and France.

question.text: The Weimar Republic was almost overthrown in this unsuccessful 1923 coup d'etat, which led to the imprisonment of Adolf Hitler.
question.answer: Beer Hall Putsch or Munich Putsch
question.clue: Its leader started it with the proclamation that "The National Revolution has begun" and this event ended after a brief firefight between insurgents and police in the Residenzstrasse.

swap.leadin: At the height of the Roman Empire, two rivers formed the border of much of the Roman frontier in Europe.
swap.text: The border began at this river's mouth on the North Sea in the Netherlands. Today, this river forms much of the Franco-German border.
swap.clue: Desire to regain lands west of this body of water by a movement headed by Georges Ernest Boulanger led to the first use of the term "revanchism."

question.leadin: The mural "My God, Help Me to Survive This Deadly Love" depicting Erich Honecker and Leonid Brezhnev kissing was painted on this structure.
question.text: Name this structure which fell after SED (S-E-D) spokesman Gunter Schabowski (GIN-ter sha-BAO-ski) mistakenly said that a new travel law would be in effect "immediately, without delay."
question.answerHtml: Berlin Wall [or Anti-Fascist Protection Rampart or Wall of Shame]
question.clue: The construction of this object created "ghost stations" in which subways on certain lines would not stop.

swap.text: Following World War II, the Trial of Major War Criminals was held in this German city. Earlier, this city was the namesake of Nazi laws passed in 1935 to protect Aryan society from Jews.
swap.clue: A speech given in this city by Julius Streicher to an audience of 700,000 appears in a propaganda film by a woman who later directed Olympia.

question.leadin: Frederick II authorized this organization to expand to Kulm in the Golden Bull of Rimini.
question.text: Name this Germanic Crusader Order that lost the 1242 Battle of the Ice to the Kievan Rus under Alexander Nevsky.
question.answerHtml: Teutonic Knights [or the Teutonic Order; prompt on the Livonian Order with “what larger organization was it part of?”]
question.clue: Their fortunes declined after Witold of Lithuania and Ladislav of Poland defeated an army led by Ulrich von Jungingen at a battle in Grunwald.

swap.text: Christina presided over the middle of Sweden's time as a Great Power, which began, roughly, with the decline of this organization. This organization of Baltic cities was dominated by Lubeck in the Middle Ages.
swap.clue: Members of this organization were expelled from their kontor at Novgorod by Ivan the Terrible.

question.leadin: This monarch's many unwise remarks included calling the English "mad as march hares" in a Daily Telegraph interview.
question.text: Name this monarch whose navy was built up rapidly by Alfred von Tirpitz. The General Staff of this monarch's army was led by Moltke the Younger.
question.answerHtml: Kaiser Wilhelm II [or Emperor William II of Germany]
question.clue: In an 1897 speech, this leader's foreign minister Bernhard von Bulow outlined how this ruler's nation wanted its "place in the sun."

swap.leadin: Identify these events orchestrated by Hitler.
swap.text: In this June 30, 1934 event, Hitler and his men carried out mass executions to purge the Nazi party, particularly the SA and its leader, Ernst Rohm.
swap.answerHtml: Night of the Long Knives [or die Nacht der langen Messer]
swap.clue: Upon his release, Vice-Chancellor von Papen's criticism of the regime was silenced.

question.text: Metternich issued these reactionary decrees in response to the assassination of August von Kozebue. They were named for the Bohemian town in which they were passed.
question.clue: The enforcement of one provision forbidding the assembly of the Burschenschaften prompted Wilhelm von Humboldt to resign from politics.

swap.text: This German Propaganda Minister was chancellor for one day after Hitler committed suicide.
swap.clue: The Sportpalast speech was given by this man, who stated that "Germany ... has no intention of bowing to this Jewish threat."

question.leadin: Identify the following about the historiography of Nazism and the Third Reich.
question.text: This personal memoir of a Nazi was written while its author was in Spandau. In it, the author recounts that he was unwillingly made Minister of Armaments after Fritz Todd died in a plane crash.
question.clue: This memoir, which claims that its author secretly sabotaged plans that would have damaged the infrastructure of his country, one of the most important primary sources in 20th century history.

swap.leadin: This entity's youth wing was called the Jugendbund.
swap.text: Name this Nazi paramilitary group that was also known as the Brownshirts. Ernst Rohm was one of the founders of this group that was destroyed during the Night of the Long Knives.
swap.clue: One member of this group wrote an anthem that began with the words "the Flag on High", and which would be renamed for him after his 1929 assassination.

question.leadin: A ship named for this man caused the last cholera outbreak in America in 1910 and 1911 while docked at Swinburne Island, near Ellis Island.
question.text: Name this Prussian field marshal who commanded the German Army's General Staff for thirty years. This general's use of mission-style directives led to a decisive victory at Koniggratz in the Austro-Prussian War.
question.answerHtml: Helmuth von Moltke the Elder [or Helmuth Karl Bernhard Graf von Moltke; prompt on von Moltke]
question.clue: Some of this commander's success is credited to his troops being armed with the technologically superior "needle gun."

swap.leadin: This activist used the pseudonym Junius to author "The Crisis in Social Democracy."
swap.text: Name this Marxist founder of Red Flag who rejected the Revisionism of Eduard Bernstein in works like The Accumulation of Capital.
swap.clue: An early work by this thinker blasted the revisionist theory of Eduard Bernstein.

question.text: The Rothschilds got their start as bankers to the ruler of this German state. Mayer Rothschild's big break came when the English started paying this state money in exchange for mercenaries to fight in America.

swap.text: The provision of the 1816 Treaty of Paris that allowed the refurbishing of the fortress of Luxembourg on France's dime also led to the construction of this German city's massive fortress. Karl Mack's army was captured at a battle near this city.

question.leadin: The name of these riots may be derived for the acronym of the Latin for "Jerusalem is lost."
question.text: Name these anti-Semitic riots that swept Bavaria in 1819, the name of which identifies the rallying cry of the crowds that was probably inspired by shepherd calls.
question.clue: This series of anti-Jewish violence which erupted across Germany in the late summer of 1819.

swap.text: The modern craft of historiography was also shaped by this German historian, who argued that historians should write of the past "as it actually happened" to create a "universal" history.
swap.clue: This 19th-century German historian and pioneer in the use of primary sources who attempted in one work to unify the experiences of the "Latin" and "Teutonic" countries of Europe.
